messages:
Maya (PM): Quick heads-up — noticed a lot of small mismatches between the in-console knowledge inlay and the public docs. Example: the inlay labels 'Pin model' while the docs call it 'Pin model version'. Confusing for new users.

Kevin (Design): Yeah I ran into that during the demo. Users expect identical phrasing. Also the inlay CTA says 'Learn more' but links to the top of the docs page, not the section about pinning. Feels like a dead end. :confused:

Sylvia (DevEx): Oof. We should deep-link to the exact anchor. Right now the docs URL we generate is /docs/models#pinning but the inlay opens /docs/models (missing the fragment).

Raj (Eng): The inlay is adding the link via the docs service with getDocLink('models') — easy fix to accept optional anchor. I can add a query param or fragment. Which anchor should we standardize on?

Maya (PM): Let's standardize on fragments that mirror the console copy. So in-console label: 'Pin model version' and fragment '#pin-model-version'. Update docs headings to include an explicit id too.

Kevin (Design): Agree. Also suggestion: change the inlay microcopy from 'Learn more' to 'See pinning docs' — more scannable in a tight UI.

Emma (A11y): Two quick accessibility nits: 1) the anchor links in the inlay open in the same frame without announce; should open a new tab with rel="noopener" and we should add an aria-label like 'Opens documentation in new tab'. 2) the inlay close button doesn't have aria-controls referencing the panel.

Raj (Eng): Good catches. I can make the link target="_blank" + rel attr and add aria-label. For aria-controls I need the panel id — do we have a predictable id?

Sylvia (DevEx): We can allocate an id pattern: "inlay-doc-panel-<route>". We'll map route 'models' -> inlay-doc-panel-models. DocBot can emit the mapping for other routes as well.

DocBot: Automated note: Added lint rule doclink-fragment-check to the docs repo that flags references to /docs/* without a fragment. (PR: https://git.internal/rdw/pulls/314)

Kevin (Design): Another UX inconsistency: the docs use sentence-case headings but the inlay uses Title Case for the same strings. Small but makes the product look unpolished in demos. We should pick one style — recommend sentence case for brevity.

Maya (PM): Action items: (1) Raj update inlay link generation to include fragments and target attr. (2) Docs team add explicit id for 'Pin model version' heading -> '#pin-model-version' and normalize case. (3) Design to update inlay copy to 'See pinning docs' and switch to sentence case. (4) Emma to add the aria-label and id conventions.

Raj (Eng): I'll take (1) and add tests. Patch will also add support for optional aria-label override when the link is generated. ETA EOD tomorrow.

Sylvia (DevEx): I'll open a small doc PR to add the heading id and a short redirect so existing links don't break. Also will add a small section in the docs style guide: 'Use sentence case for inlay copy'.

Emma (A11y): I'll write the aria guidance and add an a11y checklist item for inlays: focus management, aria-controls, aria-label on external links.

Maya (PM): Thanks — last thing: can we add a short tooltip microcopy change for keyboard users. Right now the info icon only shows on hover. Needs a keyboard focusable `button` with same tooltip content.

Raj (Eng): Yep will change it from a span to a button with role="button" and tabindex=0.

Kevin (Design): Will share updated component mockups in this thread tomorrow morning. :+1:

Maya (PM): Great. If anyone sees other phrasing mismatches in other areas (metrics, routing docs, or 'dedicated' vs 'reserved capacity') paste them here and we'll triage.

Sylvia (DevEx): Quick FYI — found a small mismatch: console shows 'Reserved capacity' but docs use 'Dedicated capacity' in one paragraph. Adding to my doc PR.

Raj (Eng): Thanks, adding a small e2e that crawls console labels vs docs headings to surface diffs.

DocBot: Reminder: Weekly docs sync is Wednesday 10am.

Maya (PM): Awesome — closing loop once PRs land. :white_check_mark:
